statement.p: Calculate \iint_{\mathcal{S}} f(x,y,z)\,dS For y = 1-z^2 \text{,} \qquad 0\le x, z\le 9 \text{;}\qquad f(x,y,z)=z \iint_{\mathcal{S}} f(x,y,z)\,dS=

static.solution: y=g( x,z ): \iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS=\iint_{\mathcal{D}} f\left(x,g( x,z ),z\right)\sqrt{1+ g_x^2+ g_z^2} \,dx \,dz \quad \mathbf{(1)} Since y=g( x,z )=1- z^2, we have g_x =0, g_z =-2z, hence: \sqrt{1+ g_x^2+ g_z^2}=\sqrt{1+4 z^2}f\left(x,g( x,z ),z\right)=z The domain of integration is the square \left[0,9\right]\times \left[0,9\right] in the xz-plane. By \mathbf{(1)} we get: \iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS = \int_0^{9} \int_0^{9} z\sqrt{1+4 z^2} \,dz \,dx=\left(\int_0^{9} 1 \,dx\right)\left(\int_0^{9} z \sqrt{1+4 z^2} \,dz\right)=9\int_0^{9} z \sqrt{1+4 z^2} \,dz We use the substitution u={1+4 z^2}, \,du= 8z \,dz to compute the integral. This gives: \iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS = 9\int_0^{9} z\sqrt{1+4 z^2} \,dz=9\int_1^{325} \frac{u^{1/2}}{8} \,du = \frac{18}3\cdot\left(\frac{{325}^{3/2}-1}{8}\right)\approx 4393.52
